title: Director, Production Engineering and Technologies, Industrialization
description:
Job Title

Director, Production Engineering and Technologies, Industrialization

Job Description

Director, Production Engineering and Technologies, Industrialization
Do you enjoy helping people grow and building strong partnerships across an organization? Do you want to shape how world-leading products go from development to production?


As our Director, Production Engineering and Technologies, Industrialization, you’ll lead an organization of about 90 people. Together, you'll make sure every new Axis product can be built and tested with high quality. The role is based on-site at our headquarters in Lund, Sweden.


Your future team
You will lead six teams, each with their own manager, all working together in Lund. These teams own the production flow in Axis product development projects. They define, develop and implement the flow, from post-PCBA (printed circuit board assembly) to a fully assembled Axis product, at our EMS partners. This includes product-specific production equipment, as well as the test modules and common sequences used in each product's test process. Our work directly affects how well and how reliably our products reach customers around the world.


You will report to the Director of Global Industrialization and be a member of the Industrialization Management Team. The management team consists of Project Quality Managers, an Industrial Lead, Packaging & Product Data Group Managers, and an EMS NPI Lead, in addition to the managers in your organization.


Who are Global Industrialization?
Our mission is to take responsibility for the industrialization activities in product development projects, ensuring that new Axis products are introduced and produced efficiently, with the right quality and optimized production costs.


We also work closely with R&D on a long-term basis to define the production capabilities and equipment needed in the future, preparing for upcoming technologies and innovations.


What you'll do as Director, Production Engineering and Technologies, Industrialization

  • Lead the strategic work to create a stronger and clearer common voice and interface towards R&D and Manufacturing.
  • Build strong partnerships and collaboration at all levels with the Production System department, which develops Axis's complex production machines.
  • Lead, coach and support six managers and, through them, an organization of approximately 90 engineers.
  • Shape the direction and strategy of Global Industrialization by taking an active role in the department's management team.
  • Attract, retain and develop talent, ensuring the organization has the capabilities needed to meet both current and future business needs.

Who are you?
You are passionate about developing leaders and enabling their teams to succeed. As a leader, you combine a strategic perspective with a genuine interest in people, creating an environment where managers and teams can perform, develop and deliver at their best.

You build strong relationships and earn the trust, support and commitment of stakeholders at all levels, both within your own organization and across neighbouring functions and departments.


To succeed in this role, you have:

  • A technical university degree in electronics, computer science, mechanical engineering or a related field.
  • At least seven years of leadership experience.
  • Experience leading technical product development or industrialization activities.
  • Fluent English, written and spoken.

Bonus points if you have:

  • Experience leading managers.
  • Experience developing production or test systems.
  • Experience in working in an international environment.
  • Fluent Swedish, written and spoken.

What Axis has to offer
We are a world leader in network video, where cutting-edge technology meets global impact.

Here, you’ll contribute to meaningful projects that shape the future of security and surveillance — developing solutions used worldwide.

As a fast-growing company, we offer exciting career opportunities. You’ll grow professionally through continuous learning, supported by a collaborative team that values creativity, innovation, and work-life balance.

Our Lund HQ Campus, including the impressive Grenden building, offers a dynamic environment with spaces crafted to encourage collaboration, whether through informal “fika” chats, formal meetings, or after-hours activities. Check it out: Axis HQ

Your well-being matters to us. We offer a range of benefits, including a company bonus, Friday cake, wellness allowance, health insurance — and even your own Axis bicycle.

To learn more about Axis, our innovative products, solutions, and vibrant company culture, explore:

Axis Career Hub
Life at Axis blog
Engineering at Axis blog
Innovation at Axis


Ready to Act?
Axis is a company realizing the benefits of a diverse workforce. We know that diversity in groups creates a better working environment and promotes creativity, something that is fundamental for our success. We welcome all applications.


We go through applications continuously so don’t wait. You may apply in Swedish or English – send in your application today!

If you have any questions about the role, please contact Åsa Strömblad, Director Global Industrialization, at asa.stromblad@axis.com or +46 (0)46 2722285

Type of Employment

Permanent Employment

Posting End Date

2026-11-21

Certain roles at Axis require background checks, which means applicable verifications will be done in these recruitments. Notice will be provided before we take any action.

About Axis Communications

We enable a smarter and safer world by creating innovative solutions for improving security and business performance. As a network technology company and industry leader, we offer solutions in video surveillance, access control, intercom, and audio systems, enhanced by intelligent analytics applications.


With around 6,000 committed employees in over 50 countries, we collaborate with partners worldwide. Together, we thrive in our friendly, open, and collaborative culture and inspire each other to think beyond the expected. United by our commitment to inclusion, diversity, and sustainability, we consistently seek to develop our skills and way of working.


Let´s create a smarter and safer world


For more information about Axis, please visit our website .

title: Trainee Fee Analyst

title: Asset Project Manager (BE)
description:
Make your mark for patients

Asset Project Manager

We are looking for an Senior Asset Project Manager who is collaborative, strategic, and results-driven to join us in our Integrated Program Management team, based in our Brussels office in Belgium.

About the role

As an Senior Asset Project Manager, you will play a key role in driving complex drug development programs from planning through execution. You will oversee critical project activities across medical, market access and stakeholder workstreams, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives, timelines and budgets.

Working closely with cross-functional teams, you will help translate program strategies into actionable plans, provide clear project visibility, manage risks and opportunities, and support informed decision-making. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to innovative healthcare solutions that aim to improve outcomes for patients worldwide while working in a dynamic and collaborative international environment.

Who you'll work with

You will be working in a team that partners with experts across drug development, medical affairs, market access, regulatory, manufacturing, safety and commercial functions.

The Integrated Program Management team enables effective planning and execution across complex development programs. You will collaborate closely with program leaders, subject matter experts and global stakeholders to align priorities, facilitate decision-making and ensure successful delivery of strategic objectives. The team values transparency, continuous improvement, knowledge sharing and an inclusive culture where diverse perspectives contribute to better outcomes.

What you'll do

• Develop and maintain integrated project plans, budgets and timelines aligned with overall program objectives.

• Coordinate cross-functional activities and ensure clear communication across global project teams and stakeholders.

• Lead scenario planning and impact assessments to support strategic and governance decision-making.

• Monitor project progress, identify risks and opportunities, and implement mitigation plans when needed.

• Provide accurate and transparent reporting on project status, milestones, budgets and key deliverables.

• Facilitate productive meetings, promote collaboration and support positive team dynamics.

• Drive the adoption of project management best practices and agile ways of working.

• Remove operational barriers and enable teams to successfully deliver critical program outcomes.

Interested? For this role we're looking for the following education, experience and skills

• Bachelor's degree in a scientific, technical or related field; advanced degree preferred.

• Minimum seven years of project management experience within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology or healthcare industry.

• Experience supporting drug development programs across clinical development, regulatory or pre-launch activities.

• Strong stakeholder management skills and experience working within complex cross-functional environments.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities, balance risks and drive projects to successful completion.

• Experience working with global and culturally diverse teams in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to support data-driven decisions.

• Project management certification or training is considered an advantage.

Are you ready to ‘go beyond’ to create value and make your mark for patients? If this sounds like you, then we would love to hear from you!

About us
UCB is a global biopharmaceutical company, focusing on neurology and immunology. We are over 9.000 people in all four corners of the globe, inspired by patients and driven by science.

Why work with us?
At UCB, we don’t just complete tasks, we create value. We aren’t afraid to push forward, collaborate, and innovate to make our mark for patients. We have a caring, supportive culture where everyone feels included, respected, and has equal opportunities to do their best work. We ‘go beyond’ to create value for our patients, and always with a human focus, whether that’s on our patients, our employees, or our planet. Working for us, you will discover a place where you can grow, and have the freedom to carve your own career path to achieve your full potential.

At UCB, we’ve embraced a hybrid-first approach to work, bringing teams together in local hubs to foster collaborative curiosity. Unless expressly stated in the description or precluded by the nature of the position, roles are hybrid with 40% of your time spent in the office.

UCB is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions will be made without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable laws.

title: Principal Systems Engineer
description:
We are seeking experienced, innovative and passionate system thinkers to join our dynamic team, working on an ambitious and pioneering programme. Imagine playing a crucial role in designing and delivering next-generation combat air systems that will set new standards in weapon integration, effectiveness and efficiency.

Salary: Up to £58,000 depending on experience

Dynamic (hybrid) working: 4 days per week on-site due to workload classification

Security Clearance: British Citizen or a Dual UK national with British citizenship

Restrictions and/or limitations relating to nationality and/or rights to work may apply. As a minimum and after offer stage, all successful candidates will need to undergo HMG Basic Personnel Security Standard checks (BPSS), which are managed by the MBDA Personnel Security Team.

What we can offer you:

  • Company bonus: Up to £2,500 (based on company performance and will vary year to year)
  • Pension: maximum total (employer and employee) contribution of up to 14%
  • Overtime: opportunity for paid overtime
  • Flexi Leave: Up to 15 additional days
  • Flexible working: We welcome applicants who are looking for flexible working arrangements
  • Enhanced parental leave: offers up to 26 weeks for maternity, adoption and shared parental leave -enhancements are available for paternity leave, neonatal leave and fertility testing and treatments
  • Facilities: Fantastic site facilities including subsidised meals, free car parking and much more…
  • Healthcare Cash Plan: The Healthcare Cash Plan benefit provides the option to claim cash back on everyday healthcare expenses such as optical, dental, health and wellbeing and more.

The Opportunity:

Join a ground-breaking programme within the Defence sector, focused on designing and delivering a cutting-edge Future Combat Air Programme for the Royal Air Force within an ambitious timeframe. This initiative is built upon a global partnership through the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), uniting the UK with international allies Italy and Japan. Together, we aim to revolutionise the integration and employment of weapons, moving beyond traditional methods to create a more dynamic and efficient approach.

We are seeking dynamic and motivated system thinkers to become integral members of our programme team. This role offers an unparalleled chance to significantly contribute to the development of advanced Weapon Effects Management capabilities. Your work will be instrumental in reducing cognitive burden and facilitating the seamless coordination of complex weaponry in the battlespace, ensuring our missions are executed with precision and effectiveness.

Join us and be part of a transformative journey that will shape the future of combat air operations.

Some of the Key Accountabilities for this role include but are not limited to;

  • Management and Delivery of key System of Systems concepting activities
  • Ownership of key requirements entities
  • Architectural processes across the project Model Based Engineering tools
  • Manage relationship with design teams to help define and convey the overall system concept, trades, fundamental design principles and constraints that balance fulfilment of the need
  • Support to cross functional assessment and analysis activities
  • Management of junior engineers and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives

What we're looking for from you:

  • An experienced systems engineer who is pro-active and readily able to work autonomously
  • Analytical Systems thinkers that are able to develop and communicate new concepts and architectures, with an understanding of the requirements/needs that drive the design
  • Ability to present and engage with a senior set of internal and external stakeholders
  • The capability to take responsibility for decisions that affect several design domains / system elements
  • Ability to influence and drive a narrative
  • Willingness to learn and deliver as part of an agile team
  • Attention to detail along with excellent organisational and communication skills

Our company: Peace is not a given, Freedom is not a given, Sovereignty is not a given

MBDA is a leading defence organisation. We are proud of the role we play in supporting the Armed Forces who protect our nations. We partner with governments to work together towards a common goal, defending our freedom.

We are proud of our employee-led networks, examples include: Gender Equality, Pride, Menopause Matters, Parents and Carers, Armed Forces, Ethnic Diversity, Neurodiversity, Disability and more…

Follow us on LinkedIn (MBDA), X (@MBDA_UK), Instagram (MBDA_UK) and Glassdoor or visit our MBDA Careers website for more information.

title: Systems Technician
description:
Are you ready to shape the future of IT? Join Integris, where integrity meets innovation, and people come first.

At Integris, we don’t just offer jobs, we offer purpose. As a nationally recognized Best Places to Work and a leader in future-ready managed services, we’re redefining how businesses experience IT. Our mission is bold: to empower clients and employees alike through secure, strategic, and scalable technology solutions.

We’re looking for talent that thrives in a culture of clarity, trust, and relentless execution, individuals who believe that IT is not just support, but a strategic advantage. If you’re passionate about innovation, driven by impact, and ready to grow with a company that puts People First, you’ll find your place here.


Job Summary:

The Systems Technician is responsible for providing frontline technical support for single end-user level issues, including personal computer, printer, Microsoft 365, Windows application, mobile device, and basic connectivity matters. This role serves as the initial point of contact for client technical assistance and is responsible for managing inquiries received through phone, email, and the client portal.

The Systems Technician provides exceptional customer service while troubleshooting and resolving support requests efficiently and effectively. This position may execute responsibilities from the service desk, the field, a client site, an Integris office, or a remote home office depending on business and client needs.

This position could participate in an on-call rotation supporting critical systems and operations outside normal business hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. Participation, availability during assigned periods, and timely response to urgent incidents are essential functions of the role.

This role is expected to build technical capability over time, follow documented processes, maintain accurate service ticket documentation, and escalate complex technical issues to Systems Administrators or Systems Engineers when appropriate. The Systems Technician contributes to a positive client experience and plays an important role in maintaining daily service delivery operations.

Job Responsibilities:

Ticket Management

  1. Work assigned tickets in order of SLA.
  2. Serve as the first point of contact for client support requests received through phone, email, and client portal.
  3. Answer inbound support calls, create service tickets, and ensure requests are properly documented, categorized, and prioritized.
  4. Troubleshoot and resolve frontline technical issues efficiently and effectively to minimize disruption to customer operations.
  5. Escalate advanced or unresolved technical issues to Systems Administrators or Systems Engineers following established escalation procedures.
  6. Document all technical work comprehensively to facilitate accurate client billing and ongoing support.

Collaboration, Communication, and Customer Service

  • Demonstrate excellent customer service skills with a focus on professionalism, responsiveness, and problem-solving.
  • Communicate clearly with clients regarding ticket status, troubleshooting steps, next steps, and resolution details.
  • Collaborate with Systems Administrators, Systems Engineers, and other technical team members to resolve client issues.
  • Participate in team meetings, training sessions, documentation efforts, and knowledge-sharing activities.
  • Follow up with clients and internal team members as needed to support timely issue resolution and a positive client experience.

Technical Support & Documentation

  • Provide frontline technical support for end-user devices, Microsoft 365 applications, and common infrastructure issues, escalating complex issues as appropriate.
  • Support the configuration, maintenance, and troubleshooting of workstations, peripheral devices, and basic server, networking, and cloud technologies under established procedures.
  • Assist with Microsoft 365 user administration, including account provisioning, password resets, licensing, and basic support for Exchange Online, Teams, and SharePoint.
  • Troubleshoot common connectivity issues involving workstations, printers, wireless networks, VPN access, and basic network services, escalating advanced networking issues when necessary.
  • Support backup verification, endpoint management, documentation, ticketing, remote management, and monitoring tools as part of daily operational activities.
  • Collaborate with Systems Administrators, Systems Engineers, and other team members to resolve client issues while continuing to develop technical knowledge and skills.
  • Follow established IT service management processes and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to deliver consistent, high-quality support.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of work performed and contribute to knowledge base articles and SOP updates as appropriate.

Professional Development & Technical Growth

  • Demonstrate curiosity and commitment to continuous learning across Microsoft technologies, networking fundamentals, service delivery, and client support.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and certification pathways that support continued growth into advanced technical responsibilities.
  • Leverage approved AI solutions responsibly to accelerate learning, improve troubleshooting efficiency, enhance documentation quality, and support better customer outcomes.
  • Develop foundational technical knowledge that prepares the employee for potential progression into Systems Administrator responsibilities.


Job Qualifications

Education/Certification Requirements:

  • Associate degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field preferred (or equivalent experience).

title: Governance and Enterprise Policy Coordinator
description:
At Conexus, we are focused on supporting our members with their needs of today, while also helping them pursue their goals for the future. It’s more than conducting a banking transaction, it’s about providing insightful content, tools, expert advice, and a full suite of products to inspire confidence in their financial decision-making. We prioritize performance excellence, and our employees champion each member’s success, ultimately contributing to a thriving province.

We are curious, courageous, confident and committed. Our values ensure we consistently deliver outstanding member experiences. As employees, we are more than just individuals who come to work each day, each role is a vital part of Conexus.

As of January 1, 2026, Conexus, Cornerstone, and Synergy credit unions have merged into one provincial credit union serving over 200,000 members in 57 branches across 50 Saskatchewan communities.

We acknowledge that our Conexus offices and facilities are located on Treaty 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10 lands. These are the traditional lands of the Cree, Dakota, Dene, Lakota, Nakota and Saulteaux peoples, as well as the homeland of the Métis.

The bigger picture

We’re looking for a highly organized and detail-oriented person to come on board as our Governance and Enterprise Policy Coordinator. Reporting to the Director, Governance, you’ll provide high-level, confidential administrative and coordination support that keeps our Board and Committees running smoothly. You’ll also play a key role in our enterprise policy lifecycle, coordinating the development, review, reporting, and maintenance of policies. If you thrive in an environment where accuracy, confidentiality, and follow-through matter, this could be the opportunity for you.

How you’ll be spending your time

  • Providing high-level, confidential administrative support to the Board and Committees.
  • Coordinating Board and Committee meetings from start to finish — scheduling, agendas, meeting packages, logistics, and follow-up actions.
  • Attending meetings to accurately record minutes, motions, decisions, and action items.
  • Serving as the primary point of contact for Board Directors on meeting logistics, documentation, and administrative inquiries, and acting as technical administrator for the board portal.
  • Supporting the Director, Governance with recurring governance matters such as director nominations and elections, new director onboarding, annual disclosures, learning and development, terms of reference, and board evaluations.
  • Coordinating director travel, expenses, Board-approved events and planning sessions, and supporting governance budget administration and year-end reconciliation.
  • Maintaining official governance records and submitting required Board and Committee materials to the regulator, where applicable.
  • Maintaining the enterprise policy framework, including standards, templates, approval workflows, version control, and disposition processes.
  • Coordinating policy review cycles and consulting with policy owners and subject matter experts to draft, review, and update policies, escalating overdue reviews, gaps, and compliance risks.
  • Preparing reports on policy status, compliance trends, and emerging risks, and supporting internal and external audits and regulatory reviews.
  • Acting as technical administrator for our policy administration technology and identifying opportunities to improve policy processes, tools, and usability.

The way people describe you

  • Trustworthy and excersie sound judgment when handling sensitive and confidential information.
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, able to prioritize competing deadlines and manage your time effectively.
  • A critical and conceptual thinker who breaks down problems and solves them collaboratively.
  • Organizationally aware, with an understanding of how governance and policy connect across the enterprise.

The experience you bring

  • 5+ years of related governance experience, supporting boards or in an administrative or policy coordination role.
  • Relevant post-secondary education, or equivalent experience.
  • Experience in governance practices, including working with boards and committees and accurately recording and producing meeting minutes and decisions.
  • Experience working in environments where accuracy, discretion, and compliance are critical.
  • Training or experience in policy system management.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft 365 (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams).

Salary range

$70,520 - $88,153 with 9% Short Term Incentive Target

Various locations are considered, some travel will be required.

Benefits and perks

The success of our members relies heavily on the performance and accomplishments of our employees. That’s why we prioritize offering our team a variety of perks and benefits designed to support their success and well-being both at work and in their personal lives. Some of these additional benefits may include, but are not limited to:

  • Generous vacation benefits, giving you time to spend on what’s most important to you
  • Competitive benefit package options, covering all aspects of personal wellness
  • Pension matching to support you towards retirement
  • Preferred rates for all your banking needs, helping to make life more affordable

We are excited to welcome candidates who bring a blend of academic, professional and volunteer experience that sets them apart. Research shows that many applicants tend to apply only when they meet every qualification of the role. However, we encourage you to explore opportunities that closely match your skillset and experience. We truly value diverse backgrounds and varied experiences, as we are dedicated to creating inclusive and diverse workplaces. This opportunity closes on November 16, 2026, so apply now! If you have questions about this position, please contact McKayla Kerr at jobs@conexus.ca.

title: ICT Technician - Currie Community High School
description:
ICT Technician
Currie Community High School

Salary: £30,188 - £34,452 (pro rata for part time and sessional)
Hours: 18 per week, 39 weeks sessional

Currie Community High School is situated to the south west of the City of Edinburgh and serves the communities of Currie, Riccarton, Juniper Green and Baberton Mains. The school has served the local community for some 350 years. The school enjoys excellent links with the local community and as a designated community high school, a quality community programme is offered. The school’s Qualification Scotland results are above both local and national averages and an extensive range of wider achievement opportunities are offered. The school is firmly committed to raising attainment and promoting positive achievement, leading to a high level of positive and sustained destinations of which Currie High has an outstanding record.

Our school values of Ambition, Respect, Equality underpin our positive culture and ethos; where celebrating success of our wonderful young people is at the heart of what we do. We also recognise the importance of our school as a community and we have been recently awarded the Gold LGBT Charter Mark which we are very proud of. We are a proactively anti racist school and are passionate about celebrating diversity, similarity and difference in our school. With over 49 languages spoken, we take the opportunity to embrace the rich cultural experiences of everyone in our school community. We are also working towards Rights Respecting School status, we hold a Silver Food For Life Catering award and have maintained Green Eco Schools status for 10 years. We were also awarded Scotland’s Most Enterprising School in 2021 and in August of this year were awarded SCQF (Scottish Credit Qualifications Framework) Gold status as a result of sector leading work in promoting curriculum pathways with purpose. Within our inclusion provision, we have an Enhanced Support Base where we support young people with severe and complex needs. This is a fantastic resource within our school where young people are not only thriving with the support they receive but also in mainstream classrooms. This is just a flavour of the innovative approaches which make Currie Community High School a unique, desirable and welcoming place to work.

We were excited to move into the first Passivhaus Secondary school in Scotland in August 2025. Our vision for the new school encompasses innovative and cutting-edge pedagogy with the development of 21st Century ready skills at the core of all we do. The school benefits from inspirational learning spaces and technology, including high-quality outdoor spaces, to enable young people to continue to become leaders of their own learning and to experience a broad, varied and bespoke curriculum.

We are seeking a skilled, positive and motivated ICT Technician to join our team. The successful applicant will support young people and school staff with their IT needs. This includes the deployment and maintenance of iPads and the running our IT Helpdesk station.

title: Strategy and Analytics Business Partner
description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Strategy & Analytics team in Internal Systems aspires to supercharge the wider Internal Systems and SDC organizations with analytics and insights. The Internal Systems and SDC org creates the engineering infrastructure and runs the internal operations that enables Stripe to succeed. Seller Systems, within this organization, builds the tools that help our sellers scale and sell our products. We deliver data-driven insights that inform business decisions, drive measurable operational improvements, and guide strategy. We are not just data analysts, we are a mix of strategic business partners, deeply strategic and/or technical operational executors. We ensure timely, reliable, high-quality data for not just Internal Systems and SDC, but for stakeholders across Stripe.

What you’ll do

In this role, you’ll be the go-to expert for your business area. You’ll partner directly with product and engineering leaders within Seller Systems and be their go-to for all things data, insights, and strategy. You’ll be hands-on and responsible for delivering critical insights, ensuring data driven decision making is at the core of what we do. You’ll partner with leadership to drive product strategy, planning, goal-setting and performance tracking. You may also scope and lead mission critical projects and execute on strategic initiatives.

Responsibilities

  • Metrics & Insights: Wrangle large, highly complex datasets using SQL into actionable insights and become the data expert for your business area. Develop metrics and large-scale dashboards to track the health of our user-facing and internal teams. Perform analyses (using SQL & other analytical tools/languages), identify trends, conduct research, build models, all to deliver objective, critical insights that can inform leadership of opportunities, risks, and strategic priorities.
  • Communicate with executives: Create narratives and documents that tell the story of your business area to influence senior Product, Engineering and Sales leadership and Stripe executive team decision making. Own executive-facing weekly, monthly or quarterly reporting.
  • Stakeholder management: Influence and drive cross-functional change by partnering with stakeholders across a wide internal network of globally distributed teams, including Ops, Finance, Data Science, Product/Engineering, and more
  • Drive operational excellence: Design, optimize and drive operational reviews and rhythm of the business. Guide the planning and goal-setting process for your business area, as well as progress checks throughout the year. Bring and consistently apply a ROI lens to all operational decisions, so we can make better-informed trade-offs
  • Conduct internal knowledge sharing sessions to strengthen the team

Who you are

You’re passionate about solving business problems and making a direct impact on business. You thrive in environments with many moving parts and quickly pick up new domain knowledge and technologies (e.g. AI). We’re seeking someone with excellent communication and advanced SQL/analytics abilities. Strong background in Sales Analytics or prior AI experience is highly preferred, though these can also be developed on the job.

Minimum requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in STEM major (i.e. Computer Science, Math, Stat, Engineering, etc.) and 4+ years of prior working experience in data analysis fields
  • Strong analytical ability, proficiency with SQL (minimum of 3 years advanced SQL) and strong understanding of data relationships
  • Experience working with extremely large datasets
  • Experience with AI tools (Claude Code, etc.) and have demonstrated measurable impact from AI in your role or in others’ around you.
  • Outstanding communication, presentation skills & stakeholder management skills
  • Experience working in or with Sales and/or Operations organizations
  • Expertise working cross-functionally and with globally distributed teams to drive business and operational goals using data
  • Ability to connect the big picture to minute details, toggling between them to set and operationalize strategy

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience working in fast-paced environments (e.g. high-growth fintech/tech company, management consulting)
  • Experience working with Product Manager and Engineering teams
  • Experience with visualization tools

title: Cabinet Officer
description:
Salary range: £43,449 - £46,161 p.a. inc. London weighting (PO1)
Contract: Permanent
Hours of work: 36 hours per week
Location: Civic centre and other locations from time to time

Are you passionate about people, the places where they live, and policymaking?

You will be working in a London borough which personifies the most exciting aspects of our capital city. Brent has many juxtapositions – from the iconic arch of Wembley to the thoroughfare of Kilburn, this is a place where economic, environmental and demographic contrasts collide in just a short walk. We are a borough which is rapidly expanding, with all of the challenges and opportunities that this change creates. It’s what makes it such a fantastic place to be a public servant and what makes us like no other place in London.

This is an exciting time to join Brent. A new Cabinet is pursuing a radical and far-reaching agenda for the borough - with a new Council Plan for the next four years now taking shape. We want to be a council that delivers locally while also making the case for wider change, as we have done through our high-profile work on gambling harms and our call for for stronger powers to protect our high streets. As a Cabinet Officer, you will be at the heart of that work, helping to shape policy and turn the Cabinet’s ambitions into action at every level.

The Post

We are recruiting for a Cabinet Officer role, which will be at the heart of Brent Council in the Leader’s Office, helping the Cabinet with executive support, policymaking, and communications.

You will:

  • Provide a full range of executive support services to at least four Cabinet Members, assisting in the preparation of agendas, reports and action taking as required.
  • Build strong internal networks to facilitate the effective relationships between Cabinet and the Corporate Management Team (CMT).
  • Support Cabinet Members to communicate their priorities to external stakeholders.

You will have unparalleled exposure to the senior politicians and sector-leading council officers, with the ability to be a part of key decisions at every turn.

Alongside your primary responsibilities, there is significant scope for development within the role, with potential to build a portfolio of policy expertise and support projects contributing to the council’s corporate priorities.

The ideal candidate will be an excellent communicator, at ease with senior politicians and officers, and with a strong interest in policymaking. It comes with the territory that you must be highly organised if you are to support multiple Cabinet Members, as well as having an eye for the details that can make or break a political career. By its very nature, you will need to be able to navigate and negotiate through situations which are complex, confidential and sensitive.

Experience is valuable and desirable, but if you can demonstrate that you understand what local government in London does and how it sits within a political, financial, and legislative context, we want to hear from you.

title: Benefits Associate - Global Benefits
description:
Job Summary

The Benefits Associate is an entry-level role within the HR Service Center that provides Tier-1 colleague support for benefits-related questions and transactions across assigned countries or populations. The role serves as a first point of contact for routine inquiries, case intake, and basic issue resolution, while coordinating with payroll, external vendors, and the Global Benefits COE to ensure timely and accurate service delivery.

This role supports day-to-day benefits administration activities, including enrollments, changes, terminations, vendor coordination, and payroll-related benefits updates. A key responsibility of the position is performing reconciliation work, including colleague census, eligibility, pension contribution, invoice, and premium reviews, to help ensure records and payments are accurate. Because reconciliation work can be more complex, structured training and process guidance will be provided.

The role is accountable for executing assigned responsibilities in a high-quality, timely manner and in alignment with service-level expectations, standard operating procedures, and operational metrics. More complex cases, exceptions, and non-routine plan matters are escalated to senior team members, payroll, vendors, or the Global Benefits COE as appropriate.

Essential Job Functions

Essential Job Functions include the following:

Customer Support and Case Management

  • Serves as a Tier-1 point of contact for colleague benefits questions, routine issue resolution, and case intake through the HR Service Center.
  • Escalates complex cases, exceptions, plan interpretation questions, and non-routine issues to senior team members, payroll, vendors, or the Global Benefits COE as appropriate.
  • Supports claim administration and collect documentation needed to facilitate submissions or follow-up with colleagues, beneficiaries, and vendors, as applicable.

Benefits Administration

  • Supports day-to-day benefits administration activities, including new hire enrollments, benefit changes, life event updates, terminations, and other colleague transactions in accordance with established procedures.
  • Collects and processes required documentation for enrollments, dependent or beneficiary updates, claims support, and other benefits transactions where applicable.
  • Supports periodic enrollment windows, flexible benefits administration, and country-specific benefit processes as assigned.

Coordination Support (Payroll, Vendors, Stakeholder)

  • Coordinates benefit-related data updates and communications with payroll, benefit vendors, and internal stakeholders to support accurate administration.
  • Coordinates benefit-related payroll inputs and follows up on payroll deduction or contribution issues to help ensure accuracy and timely resolution.
  • Supports administration of benefits or voucher programs that are not fully managed by external vendors, following defined processes and controls.

Reconciliation and Financial Administration

  • Performs reconciliation work, including colleague census, eligibility, pension contribution, invoice, and premium reviews, and follows established processes to investigate and resolve routine discrepancies.
  • Processes and reconciles benefit invoices, premium payments, allowances, reimbursements, and other assigned transactions in coordination with finance, payroll, and vendors.
  • Prepares, distributes, and reconciles eligibility, enrollment, and other recurring reports used for benefits administration and vendor processing.

Retirement Programs

  • Supports retirement and pension administration activities for designated countries or programs, including contribution updates, coordination with vendors, and related administrative follow-up, with training and guidance provided.

Process, Documentation & Continuous Improvement

  • Maintains and updates process documentation, templates, and service resources to support consistent and effective service delivery.
  • Performs additional related duties as assigned by the manager or in coordination with the Global Benefits COE.

Competencies

Required Proficiency Level

(Fundamental; Intermediate; Advanced; Thought Leader)

Action Oriented

Enjoys working hard; is action oriented and full of energy for the things he/she sees as challenging; not fearful of acting with a minimum of planning; seizes more opportunities than others.

Fundamental

Customer Focus

Is dedicated to meeting the expectations and requirements of internal and external customers; gets first-hand customer information and uses it for improvements in products and services; acts with customers in mind; establishes and maintains effective relationships with customers and gains their trust and respect.

Fundamental

Functional/Technical

Skills Has the functional and technical knowledge and skills to do the job at a high level of accomplishment.

Fundamental

Informing

Provides the information people need to know to do their jobs and to feel good about being a member of the team, unit, and/or the organization; provides individuals information so that they can make accurate decisions; is timely with information.

Fundamental

Process Management

Good at figuring out the processes necessary to get things done; knows how to organize people and activities; understands how to separate and combine tasks into efficient workflow; knows what to measure and how to measure it; can see opportunities for synergy and integration where others can’t; can simplify complex processes; gets more out of fewer resources.

Fundamental

Standard Minimimum Requirements

  • Education: High School Degree or associate’s degree
  • Experience: Entry-level position; prior experience in customer service, shared services, HR operations, benefits administration, payroll support, or other administrative work is preferred.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • High level customer service orientation and ability to communicate clearly with colleagues, vendors, and internal stakeholders
  • High level attention to detail, accuracy, and follow-through, especially when reviewing and reconciling data
  • Ability to review and analyze data to identify discrepancies and trends
  • Comfort working with data, reports, and common business software such as Excel and Word
  • Basic understanding of service metrics and data quality concepts
  • Experience with HR systems or service management tools is preferred
  • Familiarity with automated workflows or digital tools to support HR processes is a plus
  • Problem-solving skills and ability to follow structured approaches to issue resolution
  • Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information
  • Ability to work across different regions, cultures and time zones
  • Ability to communicate effectively across multiple channels (email, systems, chat)
  • Ability to work with both internal and external stakeholders with guidance
  • Ability to learn and follow defined processes, service standards, and escalation paths
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines in a service center environment
  • Ability to identify opportunities to improve processes and enhance efficiency
  • Training will be provided on Alcon benefits processes, systems, reconciliation activities, and country-specific requirements
  • The ability to fluently speak, read, write, understand and communicate in English.

title: Processing Tech I
location: Salt Lake City, Utah, United States
description:
Schedule:
7-On/7-Off A week
9:00 PM - 7:30 AM

Department: Specimen Processing 232

*Hourly rate is an estimate only which includes shift differential for nights, evenings or weekend shifts. Overall hourly rates will vary based on schedule

Primary Purpose:

Works under direct supervision to learn the proper handling of all specimens received at ARUP's central facility and/or University Division and prepares specimens for laboratory testing. The position includes such functions as matching patient information, data entry, aliquoting, and scanning documents.

About ARUP:

ARUP Laboratories is a national clinical and anatomic pathology reference laboratory and an enterprise of the University of Utah and its Department of Pathology. Based in Salt Lake City, Utah.

ARUP proudly hires top talent to create a work environment of diversity, professional growth and continuous development. Our workforce is committed to the important service we provide to over one million patients each month. We always strive for excellence and have a strong desire to have involvement with the advances in medicine and the role laboratory services plays within each patient’s life. We never forget that there is a patient behind every specimen we receive.

We are looking for individuals who want to contribute to ARUP's culture of accountability, integrity, service, and excellence. Consider joining our dynamic team.

Essential Functions:

Reads and signs all department specific Sop's and Safety Manual.

Attends Specimen Processing team and staff meetings.

Immediately processes specimens as they become available.

Enter patient demographics and process specimens/orders using the appropriate applications.

Order all tests indicated on the requisition.

Process all manual and electronically transmitted tests on submitted paperwork.

Properly comments any additional information on the requisition/packing list.

Follow department process to resolve issues when problems are identified e.g. order EXCEPT TT, EPIC follow up task, etc.

Handles and labels all specimens and paperwork appropriately.

Able to recognize and appropriate handle all specimen types per corporate and departmental procedure.

Properly documents all specimen receipt information as outlined in departmental procedures.

Properly documents the appropriate client provided information on specimen labels.

Ensures all appropriate identifiers are checked on all received specimens/paperwork and electronically. Must ensure all match and all specimens are labelled correctly.

Properly handles specimens requiring a reroute or to be shared.

Places processed specimens on the automated track, or at the appropriate temperature for manual sorting, or delivers to the testing laboratory at the proper temperature if automated delivery systems are not available.

Able to process specimens at all three temperatures and follow the appropriate procedures for all manual and electronically transmitted orders.

Properly operates the biological safety cabinet.

University Hospital Clinical Lab only: Properly operates the centrifuge.

Proficient in the Internal Test Directory (ITD) or applicable test information catalog as related to accessioning and client submissions/inquiries.

Proficient in all current departmental LIS applications and functions.

Aliquots specimens according to procedure using the proper safety equipment.

Knows ARUP and University Division laboratories and able to determine their locations, hours of operations, and general functions (or able to find such information using departmental information on Nucleus).

Ability to make sound judgement decisions or checks with Supervisor, Lead, or Workflow Coordinator when needed, before making such decisions.

Assists the management team in handling more complex processing needs including specimen searches and processing compromised shipments when needed.

Observes principles of data security and patient confidentiality. Maintains ethical standards in the performance of testing and in interactions with patients, co-workers and other health care professionals.

Adheres to all safety policies and regulations including, but not limited to, proper dress code and using proper protective clothing and other equipment.

Remains informed of all procedures pertaining to department.

Performs cleaning duties as assigned.

Assists with departmental projects.

Central Processing: Proficient in the following ARUP applications: Accessioning and Shipment Tracking.

University Division: Properly operates the centrifuge and ensures specimen acceptability and integrity per department protocol.

University Division: Correctly prepares specimens for delivery between ARUP testing facilities by creating packing list according to specimen handling requirements.

Other duties as assigned.

Physical and Other Requirements:

Stooping: Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist.

Reaching: Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.

Mobility: The person in this position needs to move between work sites and inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, etc.

PPE: Biohazard laboratory environment that requires use of personal protective equipment in accordance with CDC and OSHA regulations and company/departmental policies.

ARUP Policies and Procedures: To conduct self in compliance with all ARUP Policies and Procedures.

Abide by the Code of Conduct as outlined in the ARUP employee handbook.

Medium Work: Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 30 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.

Fine Motor Control: Picking, pinching, typing or otherwise working, primarily with fingers rather than with the whole hand as in handling.

Vision: Having close, far, and peripheral visual acuity to perform a variety of tasks such as make general observations of depth and distance.

Color Vision: Perception of and ability to distinguish colors

Performance Expectations: Regular and reliable attendance. Reliable and dependable performance. Ability to work well with others. Ability to work all required overtime.

title: Research Associate - AI Evaluations
description:
About Karya:

Why was Karya on the cover of the Time Magazine , highlighted by Satya Nadella , and chosen by Google as its partner for Project Vaani?

In part, because Karya is on a mission to provide AI enabled earning and learning opportunities to economically underserved communities, thereby building a pathway out of poverty for them. Karya achieves this while also delivering high quality, timely, and price competitive data to its clients.

Karya's workers make at least 20 times the Indian minimum wage and through our one-of-a-kind digital work platform, we have delivered over 40 million digital tasks and are poised to positively impact over 100 thousand workers by the end of the year. In the coming years, our goal is to rapidly scale our impact by bringing economic opportunities to millions of underserved users in India.

About The Role

At Karya, we’re building AI evaluation systems that measure and understand whether AI systems actually work for the communities they’re meant to serve. We’re looking for a Research Associate to help design and run community-facing research that shapes how AI systems are evaluated. You’ll contribute to research workstreams end to end: shaping the research design, building toolkits, running fieldwork, and turning what you learn into evaluation frameworks and datasets. You’ll contribute to a range of evaluation projects across the team. These could include building a gender-bias benchmark for AI chatbots in domains like agriculture; conducting grounded research into what people in India actually use AI for, in which languages and in what contexts, to build evaluation categories from real use; or contributing to conceptual and methods work on what “community” and “participatory” should mean in AI evaluation, pressure-tested against fieldwork with Karya’s worker community.

The role suits someone with roots in social science who has worked where technology, impact and AI meet, and who cares about gender equity and doing research with communities.

Concretely, this means:

  • Contribute to research design, including research questions, methods, site selection and sampling, working closely with project leads
  • Build and adapt research toolkits: discussion guides, oral consent scripts in local languages, training materials and feedback tools
  • Plan and conduct focus group discussions, interviews and pilots with communities, including participant recruitment and field logistics
  • Coordinate with field teams during data collection, keeping research consent-first and respectful of participants’ time and context
  • Clean, cull and analyse qualitative and quantitative data through a gender and intersectional lens
  • Synthesise insights into findings that strengthen evaluation frameworks, datasets and toolkits
  • Contribute to desk research, reports and external outputs
  • Support project management by tracking timelines, deliverables and decisions across internal teams (Ops, Tech) and external partners

Why This Role

You’ll be embedded with the Evaluations team within Karya’s tech team, where social science and engineering work as one practice. We believe you can’t judge whether an AI system works for people without understanding both the people and the system, and how social and technical structures shape each other. So researchers and engineers on our team work closely together, each bringing what the other can’t. Your research will shape what gets built: community insights become evaluation categories, fieldwork defines what a good answer looks like, and research design decides whose voices go into a dataset. Working alongside engineers, you’ll learn how AI systems are built, tested and deployed, and how they reach the communities we work with. title: Burn Table Operator - Night Shift
description:

Location: East Houston

Position Summary
At North Shore Steel, precision begins long before fabrication. As a Burn Table Operator, you will play a critical role in transforming raw steel plate into accurately cut components that serve as the foundation for our customers' projects.

Operating a CNC Plasma and Oxy-Fuel Cutting System, you will be responsible for safely producing quality parts that meet customer specifications while supporting production schedules and maintaining high standards for accuracy, efficiency, and safety.

Production Operations

Operate the CNC Plasma Burn Table in accordance with production schedules and work instructions.
Review work orders, drawings, and nesting layouts prior to processing material.
Verify material grade, dimensions, and heat information match production requirements.
Monitor cutting operations to ensure quality, efficiency, and safe operation.
Inspect finished parts for dimensional accuracy and conformance to specifications.
Separate, identify, and organize completed parts for downstream processing.

Quality & Accuracy

Read and interpret blueprints, drawings, and work orders.
Verify cut quality, edge condition, hole accuracy, and overall dimensional compliance.
Identify potential production issues before material is processed.
Report quality concerns, equipment issues, or drawing discrepancies to supervision promptly.
Maintain accurate part identification and traceability throughout the production process.

Equipment & Work Area Management

Perform daily equipment inspections and basic preventative maintenance tasks.
Monitor consumables and notify supervision when replacement parts or supplies are needed.
Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area.
Assist with troubleshooting minor operational issues.
Coordinate material movement with crane operators and other production personnel.

Teamwork & Continuous Improvement

Participate in safety meetings, training programs, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Support cross-training efforts and assist in training new team members when requested.
Communicate effectively with supervisors, schedulers, crane operators, and production personnel to maintain workflow.
Contribute to a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and teamwork.

What It Takes to Be Successful
Required Qualifications

Minimum of 2 years of experience operating CNC plasma metal processing equipment.
Ability to read and interpret production drawings and work orders.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality.
Basic computer skills and ability to work with CNC production systems.
Ability to safely work around overhead cranes, moving material, and manufacturing equipment.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience operating Kinetic, Burny, Hypertherm, or similar CNC cutting systems.
Experience processing structural steel plate or heavy industrial materials.
Experience using overhead cranes and material handling equipment.
Familiarity with plate processing, fabrication, or steel service center operations.

Why Join North Shore Steel
At North Shore Steel, every piece of steel we process supports projects that help build critical infrastructure across the country. We believe in creating opportunities for employees to learn, grow, and contribute to a team committed to safety, quality, and exceptional customer service.

  • Familiarity with market intelligence tools and the ability to translate data into sourcing strategy.

Working at ICEYE

As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.

Benefits

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion

Soft Skills

title: Head of Propulsion Battery System (all genders)
description:
Your Mission:

Join VÆRIDION on our journey to develop the world’s first electric nine-seater aircraft.

As Head of Propulsion Battery System (PBS), you will lead VÆRIDION’s PBS department and hold overall technical accountability for the Microliner’s propulsion battery system. The propulsion battery system encompasses the battery cells and packs, the battery management system, high-voltage power distribution and protection, thermal management, charging, and all interfaces to the aircraft, the electric propulsion system and the ground infrastructure.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, you will lead a multidisciplinary organisation of around 20 engineers, and growing, spanning electrical systems architecture, airborne electronics, airborne software, cell technology, high-voltage electrical systems, mechanical design and integration, and thermal management. You will set the technical direction, build the organisation and its development processes, and take the propulsion battery system from concept through development, qualification and certification to production readiness.

You will also own the intellectual property strategy for the propulsion battery system, represent VÆRIDION on technical matters towards authorities, industrial partners and funding bodies, and contribute your expertise to other key technologies of the Microliner.

Your Day-to-Day:

  • Hold overall technical accountability for the propulsion battery system across its full lifecycle, from concept and architecture through development, validation & verification, qualification and certification to entry into service.

  • Define and maintain the propulsion battery system architecture together with the Electrical Systems Architect, ensuring that requirements are correctly allocated, interfaces are controlled, and trade-offs between safety, mass, energy, power, cost and certifiability are made deliberately and documented.

  • Lead, develop and scale the Energy Storage System department, comprising the Airborne Electronics, Airborne Software, Cell Technology, HV Electrical Systems, Mechanical Design & Integration and Thermal Management teams.

  • Recruit, coach and develop team leads and engineers, define clear roles and responsibilities, and align resourcing and hiring plans with the needs of the Microliner programme.

  • Take ownership of key technical decisions, chair design and gate reviews, and escalate programme-level technical risks to the CTO with clear options and recommendations.

  • Own the safety-driven design of the propulsion battery system, including thermal-runaway containment, high-voltage safety and fault tolerance, and work closely with Safety and Systems Engineering on FHA, PSSA, SSA and common-cause analyses.

  • Establish and maintain development processes in line with ARP4754A/B, ARP4761/ARP4761A, DO-254, DO-178C, DO-160G and DO-311A, ensuring traceability, configuration control and verification evidence appropriate to the allocated Design Assurance Levels.

  • Shape the certification approach for the propulsion battery system in cooperation with Certification and Airworthiness and represent the ESS team in technical discussions with EASA, including Stage of Involvement (SOI) and compliance reviews.

  • Own the integration of the propulsion battery system with the aircraft, the electric propulsion system and the charging and ground infrastructure, including the definition and control of all associated interface requirements.

  • Develop and execute the intellectual property strategy for the propulsion battery system: identify patentable innovations, lead invention disclosures and work with patent counsel on filings, freedom-to-operate assessments and prior-art reviews.

  • Own the PBS department budget, including planning, forecasting and cost control for personnel, hardware, test campaigns and external services.

  • Select and manage key technology suppliers and partners, including cell suppliers, electronics manufacturing partners and suppliers of materials and components, ensuring technical performance, quality and security of supply.

  • Define and oversee the propulsion battery system test strategy, from component and subsystem testing through system-level, environmental, abuse and certification testing, together with the required laboratory and test infrastructure.

  • Prepare the transition from development to series production together with Manufacturing, Quality and Supply Chain, applying design-for-manufacture, design-for-assembly and design-for-test principles.

  • Represent VÆRIDION on technology matters towards authorities, industrial partners, research institutions and funding bodies, and support the preparation and execution of publicly funded research and development projects.

  • Contribute technical expertise to other key technologies of the Microliner and the company’s long-term technology roadmap.

  • Foster an engineering culture defined by technical rigour, accountability, open communication and continuous improvement.

Your Profile:

  • Master’s degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Automotive, Electrochemistry or a related discipline.

  • 15 or more years of professional experience developing complex, safety-critical systems, including at least five years leading multidisciplinary engineering teams.

  • Proven experience developing high-voltage battery systems for aerospace or automotive applications, from concept through qualification and production.

  • Sound technical understanding of lithium-ion cell technology, battery management systems, high-voltage electrical systems, thermal management and the mechanical integration of battery packs, with the ability to make well-founded decisions across these disciplines.

  • Experience with thermal-runaway containment, high-voltage safety and functional safety concepts for battery systems.

  • Practical experience with aerospace development and certification standards, including ARP4754A/B, ARP4761/ARP4761A, DO-254, DO-178C, DO-160G and DO-311A, is strongly preferred. Familiarity with CS-23 certification is advantageous.

  • A track record of building and scaling engineering organisations, including recruitment, development of team leads and the introduction of structured development processes.

  • Experience with budget responsibility, supplier selection and the management of strategic technology partners.

  • Experience generating and protecting intellectual property, including invention disclosures and collaboration with patent counsel.

  • Experience representing technical programmes towards authorities, partners, funding bodies and other external stakeholders.

  • The ability to communicate complex technical matters clearly to engineers, executive management and external stakeholders.

  • A structured, decisive and hands-on leadership style, with the ability to perform in a fast-paced start-up environment.

  • Fluent English-language skills are essential; German-language skills are beneficial.

We recognize that women and other under-represented groups are often overlooked in our industry. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every listed qualification, we still encourage you to apply. Talent and potential can’t always be captured in a checklist.

Why us?

  • Be part of an ambitious team determined to shape the future of aviation.

  • We are an in-office company, but we value flexibility and trust employees to manage their schedules responsibly. This may include occasional remote work or adjusting hours to accommodate personal commitments.

  • Subsidized EGYM Wellpass membership: your (mental) health is important for us.

  • Enjoy a subsidized lunch with a 5€ company contribution per meal on office days.

  • Become a part of our success with virtual stock options.

  • Choose the option that suits your needs: either a free charging station for your electric car or a public transport job ticket as part of the Deutschlandticket.

  • Lease a high-quality bicycle or e-bike through our JobRad program and benefit from tax advantages. Whether for your daily commute or personal use, enjoy more mobility and sustainability.

  • Pension scheme to support your long-term financial security.

  • Work in one of our offices in Munich or Delft. Enjoy the modern Balan Campus in Munich or work inside the aerospace ecosystem at TU Delft.

  • Boost your professional as well as personal growth executing your own ideas and independent projects.

  • Join our internal social events and retreats (e.g. cooking, game nights, sports).

VÆRIDION was founded in 2021 to transform regional air travel with the Microliner, a 100% electric commercial aircraft. By delivering the most energy-efficient aircraft, we are building the future where clean, safe, and affordable electric aviation seamlessly connects people and businesses. We’re bringing together the brightest minds in aerospace, automotive engineering, and business to disrupt the aviation industry.

title: AR Manager
description:
At Alcon, we are driven by the meaningful work we do to help people see brilliantly. We innovate boldly, champion progress, and act with speed as the global leader in eye care. Here, you’ll be recognized for your commitment and contributions and see your career like never before. Together, we go above and beyond to make an impact in the lives of our patients and customers. We foster an inclusive culture and are looking for diverse, talented people to join Alcon.


Role Purpose

Lead the Accounts Receivable team for Alcon China and own the end-to-end account receivable process and accounting. This covers customer credit control and collection management, tax invoicing, treasury, customer rebate accounting, and AR accounting and reporting. The role makes sure AR accounting judgements and positions comply with the Alcon Manual of Accounting and IFRS/PRC GAAP. It also delivers high-quality, on-time AR closing and group/statutory reporting, working with the R2R, Tax and AGS in the FRA team and with Customer Operations, BPA, Sales and global function.

Major Accountabilities

1. Customer Credit Control & Collection Management

  • Own the credit control and collection process. This includes credit limit governance, overdue and aged AR monitoring, collection targets and DSO/overdue KPIs.
  • Partner with collectors on high-risk customers, disputes, escalations and credit holds.
  • Review the bad debt / ECL provision and accounting estimates, and ensure the results are followed up.

2. Tax Invoicing

  • Ensure tax invoicing is compliant, accurate and timely, including e-invoicing/Golden Tax requirements, credit/debit notes and red-letter invoices.
  • Work with the Tax team on VAT and other tax impacts of AR transactions, and on audit and tax authority inquiries.

3. Treasury & Cash Management

  • Oversee cash application, bank reconciliation, collection and payment flows, and IC settlement and payment compliance.
  • Support cash forecasting and working capital improvement with Treasury and the business.

4. Customer Rebate Accounting

  • Own the customer rebate accounting process and SOP. This includes rebate accruals, true-ups, residual balance clean-up and settlement follow-up.
  • Make sure revenue deferrals and sales deductions are treated correctly (including material-right assessments) under IFRS 15.
  • Coordinate with BPA, Customer Operations and Sales Operations on rebate programs, approvals and contract status. Complete AFCM control testing.

5. AR Accounting, Reporting & Closing

  • Deliver high-quality, on-time AR closing, group reporting and statutory reporting, with discrepancies resolved properly.
  • Monitor periodic balance sheet reviews, SOP compliance and the accounting estimates of the AR team, and ensure review results are acted on.
  • Act as the local process owner for AR, continuously improving the process as business and reporting requirements change.
  • Maintain AR-related documentation. Give technical support on accounting judgements to the team, and support internal/external audits.

6. People Leadership

  • Lead, coach and motivate the AR team, and build strong accounting knowledge, communication and problem-solving skills.
  • Set clear objectives, give regular feedback, and develop succession and continuity within the team.

7. Other

  • Any other duties or projects commensurate with the grade and level of responsibility of the role.

Background & Requirements

Education: Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance. CICPA/ACCA preferred.

Language: Fluent English (spoken and written)

Experience (key requirements):

  • At least 8 years of accounting experience in a multinational company (MNC), covering AR/O2C.
  • At least 2 years in a people manager role, with proven ability to lead and develop a team.
  • Hands-on experience in credit control and collection management, and in customer rebate accounting.
  • Working knowledge of tax invoicing (VAT/e-invoicing) and treasury/cash management.
  • Strong financial accounting and reporting skills, familiar with IFRS and PRC GAAP.
  • Big-4 audit background preferred.
  • SAP experience is a plus.

Competencies:

  • Good interpersonal, communication, negotiation, problem-solving and analytical skills. Able to influence cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Accurate, reliable, accountable and pro-active, with a strong sense of confidentiality.
  • Able to work under pressure with tight deadlines and manage multiple tasks.
  • Willing to take over responsibilities.

Who We Are:

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world.
